$comment: Production record, 29 Aug 2026, UNMODIFIED. DIALECT C, and ACCEPTED since 8 Sep 2026: ZC answered on 4 Sep with 'make it work for all the known dialects', which reversed the earlier one-dialect decision. It moved here from invalid/ when the schema gained the closed three-dialect enumeration, and the $expect: writer-dlq marker it used to carry went with it. READ THE data BLOCK BEFORE WRITING ANY PARSER AGAINST 'dialect C': this is NOT 'everything prefixed'. Fifteen counters are lora_-prefixed (lora_rx_nr_pkts), while fsk_received and timespan arrive BARE, and rx_type_arol is absent entirely. A branch written from the prose rather than from this record rejects the traffic it was written to accept. It carries version:1, the same as the other two dialects, so nothing on the record could have discriminated it. The Writer normalises it into the SAME typed columns as dialects A and B - one stored shape, one API shape, with the dialect carried as the metric label records_lorastats_dialect{dialect} and never as a column. NOTE: production sends tenant == maintenant == "mzc", which is exactly the trap: only tenant isolates, and equal values cannot reveal a filter on the wrong field. This fixture is kept byte-faithful because its job is to be a production regression guard; it is NOT an isolation test. The *-tenant-isolation-pair.json fixtures, where the two values deliberately differ, remain the only isolation guards.
